display_title: FBI Arrests California Woman for Alleged Spying
display_title_he: ה-FBI עצרה אישה מקליפורניה בחשד לריגול
short_summary: Federal authorities arrested a California woman at Los Angeles International Airport, accusing her of acting as an unregistered foreign agent by surveilling the family of Taiwan's president for China.

sources.title: FBI arrests a woman accused of spying on Taiwan leader's family for China

paragraphs: Federal law enforcement authorities in the United States arrested a California resident at Los Angeles International Airport as she attempted to board a flight to China. According to statements from the Federal Bureau of Investigation and federal prosecutors, the 34-year-old suspect faces allegations of operating as an unregistered foreign agent on behalf of the Chinese government.

Investigators stated that the accused individual traveled to Seattle at the direction of Chinese handlers to conduct surveillance on a relative of Taiwan's leadership. Court documents and official statements allege that she captured photographs, recorded videos, and collected license plate details concerning the target and his family members, while employing specialized tradecraft to evade detection.

Taiwan's presidential office characterized the situation as a clear instance of transnational repression. A spokesperson expressed strong condemnation toward behavior that undermines human rights and national sovereignty, while conveying gratitude to American authorities for safeguarding Taiwanese citizens. Officials identified the target as a United States resident and a son of Taiwanese President Lai Ching-te.

Representatives for the Chinese government did not immediately provide comments regarding the arrest, and the diplomatic mission in Washington remained unavailable. The legal proceedings highlight ongoing geopolitical tensions surrounding Taiwan's distinct political identity and Beijing's territorial claims over the island democracy.

facts.fact: FBI arrested Wanying Zhang at Los Angeles International Airport on Sunday before a planned flight to China.
Zhang, 34, of Irvine, California, was charged with acting as an unregistered foreign agent for China.
Authorities alleged Zhang surveilled the son of Taiwan's President Lai Ching-te and his family, capturing photos, videos, and license plate information.
Taiwan's presidential office denounced the incident as a case of transnational repression and thanked the US government.
